analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Birla Real Estate fails on every Magic Formula criterion: it is a real estate company (explicitly excluded from the Magic Formula due to capital structure distortion), is currently loss-making (Net loss INR 157 Cr in FY25, operating income collapsed to INR 16 Cr), and has seen revenue decline at a -20.5% CAGR over 8 years. There is no EBIT to work with, and the debt load has tripled in two years.
key_strengths: Aditya Birla group brand affiliation provides some credibility and access to capital markets
Forward P/E of 11.36 suggests the market anticipates a recovery in earnings — though the path is unclear
Promoter holding at 50.21% indicates skin in the game
key_risks: EBIT essentially zero (INR 16 Cr operating income, FY25) on INR 1,219 Cr revenue — ROIC is negative
Borrowings surged from INR 1,059 Cr (FY23) to INR 5,490 Cr (FY25) — a 5x spike in two years, raising solvency risk
Operating cash flow deeply negative at -INR 1,293 Cr in FY25; FCF of -INR 1,413 Cr — company is burning cash at an accelerating pace
red_flags: Real estate sector: Magic Formula explicitly excludes this industry — capital employed metrics are structurally distorted
Revenue CAGR of -20.5% over 8 years — this business is shrinking dramatically, not growing
Negative EBIT: Magic Formula cannot be computed; earnings yield is essentially 0.08% (INR 16 Cr EBIT / ~INR 19,958 Cr EV)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
ABREL is disqualified on first principles: real estate companies are excluded from Magic Formula analysis because project-based revenue recognition, land inventory, and development accounting make EBIT/EV and ROIC metrics meaningless comparators. Even setting that aside, FY25 operating income of just INR 16 Cr on nearly INR 1,220 Cr revenue implies an operating margin near zero — a dramatic collapse from INR 924 Cr in FY17. The company is not merely cheap; it is fundamentally impaired.

The balance sheet tells an alarming story: total assets have nearly doubled to INR 17,184 Cr (FY25) while total equity fell to INR 3,780 Cr, with borrowings surging to INR 5,490 Cr. Operating cash flow ran -INR 1,293 Cr in FY25 funded entirely by fresh borrowings (financing CF +INR 2,218 Cr). ROCE is -0.16%, ROE is -2.45%. There is no scenario where this passes a Magic Formula screen.
